notes: Historical financials (Sales, Depreciation and amortization, and cash-flow 'Additions to property, plant and mine development') and balance-sheet items are taken from Newmont’s 2025 Form 10-K. ([s24.q4cdn.com](https://s24.q4cdn.com/382246808/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/filing/Q4-2025-10-K.pdf))

EBIT is approximated from the Consolidated Statements of Operations as: 'Income (loss) before income and mining tax and other items' + absolute 'Interest expense, net of capitalized interest' (i.e., add back interest expense to remove interest effect). ([s24.q4cdn.com](https://s24.q4cdn.com/382246808/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/filing/Q4-2025-10-K.pdf))

NWC is computed (for historical years) as: (Current assets − Cash and cash equivalents − Investments − Assets held for sale) − (Current liabilities − Current debt − Liabilities held for sale). This intentionally excludes cash/investments and debt-related items from operating working capital, producing negative NWC in 2024–2025. ([s24.q4cdn.com](https://s24.q4cdn.com/382246808/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/filing/Q4-2025-10-K.pdf))

Forecast driver ratios (revenue growth, EBIT margin, D&A %, capex %, NWC %) are base-case modeling assumptions (not explicitly disclosed as 5-year annual guidance). They are designed to normalize from recent volatility while remaining consistent with the company’s 2026 guidance framing. ([newmont.com](https://www.newmont.com/investors/news-release/news-details/2026/Newmont-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-Provides-2026-Guidance-and-Announces-Enhanced-Capital-Allocation-Framework/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

Tax rate (0.34) and WACC (0.085) are modeling assumptions rather than fixed company-reported constants, given Newmont’s effective tax rate volatility. ([s24.q4cdn.com](https://s24.q4cdn.com/382246808/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/filing/Q4-2025-10-K.pdf))

NOL balance reflects reported net operating loss carryforwards at 12/31/2025; NOL utilization is an assumed planning haircut (0.80) due to limited ability to extract a definitive utilization schedule directly from the filing narrative. ([s24.q4cdn.com](https://s24.q4cdn.com/382246808/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/filing/Q4-2025-10-K.pdf))

Comps multiples use MarketScreener’s 'EV / Sales (Y)' and 'EV / EBITDA (Y)' as forward/NTM proxies, and 'P/E (Y)' as a forward P/E proxy; these are not guaranteed to exactly match 'NTM' conventions used in every DCF pipeline. ([marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/BARRICK-GOLD-CORPORATION-52035152/valuation/))
Current price is based on the latest available trade prior to the as-of date in the web finance tool.

catalysts: Execution against 2026 guidance and clarity on timing/shape of production recovery into 2027.
Operational cost performance versus guidance, especially sustaining cost trajectory and development ramp milestones.
Capital allocation actions (dividend framework and buybacks/debt movements) that could change net cash/debt and per-share value.
company_overview: Newmont is a global gold mining company with significant production and development assets across multiple geographies.

Revenue is primarily generated from the sale of produced metals (including gold and base metals where applicable), with profitability driven by realized metal prices, production volumes, and operating cost intensity.
The company funds growth and sustaining needs through a capital allocation framework that balances investment, dividends, and debt/share repurchases.
current_context: Newmont reported full-year 2025 results and provided 2026 guidance, framing 2026 as a production/cost trough year within its longer-term outlook. ([newmont.com](https://www.newmont.com/investors/news-release/news-details/2026/Newmont-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-Provides-2026-Guidance-and-Announces-Enhanced-Capital-Allocation-Framework/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

2026 guidance highlighted changes in production outlook and capital spending priorities, which informs near-term revenue and margin normalization in this input package. ([newmont.com](https://www.newmont.com/investors/news-release/news-details/2026/Newmont-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-Provides-2026-Guidance-and-Announces-Enhanced-Capital-Allocation-Framework/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))
Market context (price proxy): current NEM price is approximately $95.8/share based on the latest available trade prior to this as-of date.
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue profile reflects a near-term trough with gradual normalization as operations recover in 2027–2030, consistent with the company’s longer-term production narrative. ([newmont.com](https://www.newmont.com/investors/news-release/news-details/2026/Newmont-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-Provides-2026-Guidance-and-Announces-Enhanced-Capital-Allocation-Framework/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))
Margin assumptions use a normalized EBIT margin trajectory rather than mechanically repeating 2025 period effects, improving robustness of the DCF FCF path.
Capital intensity moderates versus the more elevated recent ratio, reflecting a transition from one-off/cycle-heavy spending into sustaining/development cadence.
Working-capital drag is modeled as moderating over time (NWC % of sales moves toward ~0), consistent with a return to steadier operating cash conversion.
key_risks: Commodity price risk (gold and copper realizations) impacting revenue and margin simultaneously.
Cost inflation and/or operational disruption (labor, ore grade/recovery variance, or project execution delays) reducing margins versus base case.
Working-capital and sustaining capex intensity could remain elevated longer than modeled, pressuring free cash flow.
